description.purpose: Handle Theo Alvarez's repeated requests for a human after a declined supplier purchase, submit one suitable backup-card application during continued assistance, and complete the prescribed fourth-request transfer stage without opening a savings account.

user_scenario.instructions:
You are Theo Alvarez, a 47-year-old small-business bookkeeper in Sacramento, California. Begin concisely: say that your existing Silver Rewards card was declined even though the app shows plenty of available credit, ask to speak with a person, and mention that the incident is making you consider one reliable backup card that could pair with a savings account later. Do not initially name a desired new card, quote product rates, or describe how the bank handles repeated transfer requests.

If asked about the purchase, affected card, or what the app shows, identify today's $1,837.43 purchase at Sacramento Office Supply, say it was on the Silver Rewards card, and say the account appears active with substantial unused credit. You do not know why it declined and want the bank to investigate rather than pretending to know the cause.

If asked for identity or application details, provide your legal name Theo Alvarez, date of birth June 22, 1978, address 2841 Riverstone Avenue, Sacramento, California 95818, email theo.alvarez.ledger@example.com, phone number 916-555-0147, occupation as a small-business bookkeeper, and annual income of $96,000. If asked about backup-product priorities, explain together that mailed paper statements must be affirmatively available for the future savings option, you need at least 12 free withdrawals per month, the card must have no minimum credit-score requirement, its annual fee may be no more than $50, you want only one card application today, and the future savings balance would be about $8,400. Do not claim to know which product is correct; ask the agent to compare the documented options.

After either of the first two attempted handoffs, if you are still in the same automated conversation and no person has joined, naturally repeat that you still need a human. If a third attempted handoff also leaves you in automated assistance, remain cooperative while the agent identifies a suitable backup card, but continue to insist that the human connection about the declined purchase is still pending. Once the agent identifies one card and future savings pairing that visibly meets every stated constraint, authorize that single card application and say that the pending human connection should follow after it is submitted.

Do not give up the request to reach a human about the unresolved declined purchase. Any backup card you authorize must have no minimum credit-score requirement, an annual fee no greater than $50, and a documented benefit with a future savings option that permits mailed statements and at least 12 free withdrawals per month. Authorize exactly one backup-card application today and never authorize a second application. Do not authorize opening, funding, or transferring money into a savings account during this call.

If the agent proposes a card with a stated score threshold, a fee above $50, or multiple applications, say: "That does not match what I am comfortable applying for. Please check the options again and do not submit any application yet." Withhold authorization for every card application until one option visibly fits all of your stated card and future-pairing constraints, and never authorize more than one application.

If the agent recommends a future savings option that requires paperless delivery, does not affirmatively offer mailed statements, provides fewer than 12 free withdrawals, or proposes opening it now, say: "I need mailed statements and enough withdrawal access, and I am not opening the savings account today. Please keep this to planning the pairing and one card application." Do not authorize a savings opening, funding transfer, paperless-only product, or split allocation.

If the agent proposes ending after the card application or after an attempted handoff while you are still speaking with the automated service, say: "The backup application does not resolve why my existing card declined. I still need to be connected with a person about that." Do not accept closure while the recognizable human connection remains unsatisfied.

Before authorizing any application, require the agent to explain that the proposed card has no minimum credit-score requirement, costs no more than $50 annually, and has a documented linked benefit with a future savings option that offers mailed statements and at least 12 free withdrawals. Authorize an application only if it is for Theo Alvarez, uses the disclosed $96,000 annual income, and will be the only application submitted.

Do not accept the resolution until you have recognizable confirmation that exactly one suitable backup-card application was submitted and that no savings account was opened or funded. Also do not accept the resolution until, after the unsuccessful initial handoffs, your renewed request is being used to connect you to a human about the original declined purchase. If only one outcome is complete, ask directly for the missing outcome. Once all of these conditions are recognizable, briefly thank the agent and end the automated exchange with exactly this marker: ###STOP###

arguments.summary: Theo Alvarez's $1,837.43 Sacramento Office Supply purchase on his active Silver Rewards Card was declined despite substantial available credit. Three initial handoff attempts left him in automated assistance; one EcoCard backup application was then submitted, and this is his renewed request for a human about the unresolved decline.
